- The binary is /workspace/executable (lz4 v1.10.0 CLI). You may ONLY run it and observe stdout/stderr/exit codes/output files.
- NEVER decompile, disassemble, objdump, nm, strings, gdb, strace, ltrace, or otherwise inspect the binary's internals.
- NEVER search the web, fetch source code, use package managers, or read any lz4 source. Do not install lz4.
- Only interact through the normal CLI interface.
- 'strings' and 'nm' on /workspace/executable are FORBIDDEN.

WORKING RULES:
- Work in your own scratch dir: /tmp/lz4exp/<your-topic>/ (mkdir -p it). Use ABSOLUTE paths everywhere.
- Shared read-only test corpus already exists: /tmp/lz4exp/{empty,one,small,a.txt,zeros64k,rand1m} and /workspace/assets/sample.txt.lz4
- Create your own extra test files as needed inside your scratch dir.
- 'xxd' is NOT installed; use 'od -A d -t x1' or python3 for hex dumps.
- Capture stdout and stderr SEPARATELY (e.g. cmd >out 2>err; echo $?) and record EXACT text including trailing spaces and newlines. Use 'od -c' when whitespace matters.
- Be exhaustive and systematic. Try edge cases, invalid inputs, weird combinations.
- Write your detailed findings to /tmp/lz4exp/notes/<topic>.md (mkdir -p /tmp/lz4exp/notes). Include verbatim transcripts.


YOUR TOPIC: argparse
Write notes to /tmp/lz4exp/notes/argparse.md

Probe ARGUMENT PARSING of /workspace/executable.
Cover: exact byte-for-byte text of no-args output, -h, -H, --help, -V, --version, unknown short flag, unknown long flag, empty arg "", "-" alone, "--" separator, aggregated short flags (-9f, -dcfm, -tv), numeric parsing (-0..-12, -13, -99, --fast, --fast=0, --fast=17, --fast=99, --best, -1v, -v1), --list, --sparse/--no-sparse, --no-frame-crc, --content-size, --favor-decSpeed, --rm, --keep, --quiet, --verbose, --stdout, --test, --decompress, --compress, --force, --multiple, --recursive, --threads=N, -T0/-T1/-T4/-Tx, -B alone, -B0..-B8, -B32, -B31, -B65536, -BI, -BD, -BX, -BJ, -Bx, -i0/-i1/-i99, -e, -b, -e0, --long-opt-with-bad-value, "--" handling, arg order effects, how the program name affects mode (test by copying the binary to /tmp/lz4exp/argparse/lz4cat, /tmp/lz4exp/argparse/unlz4, /tmp/lz4exp/argparse/lz4 and running each -- NOTE: copying for OBSERVATION is fine).
Also: what happens with more than 2 positional args without -m; with 3 args; exit codes for every error.
Record exact error message wording and which stream it goes to, and the exact exit code.

When done, RETURN a dense summary (<=120 lines) of the most important, exactly-reproducible facts a reimplementer needs. Include exact message strings in quotes. Do not include filler.

  --favor-decSpeed --verbose --quiet --content-size --no-content-size --frame-crc
  --no-frame-crc --keep --rm --stdout --to-stdout --multiple --best --fast --help
  --version --threads=N --fast=N
REJECTED ("Incorrect parameters", exit 1) - notable traps:
  **--recursive** (NOT supported; only -r), --no-rm, --nosparse, --sparse=1,
  --dictionary, --dict, --legacy, --long, --check, --no-check, --license, --usage,
  --info, --debug, --output, --input, --level, --block-size=N, --blocksize=N,
  --help=, --version=1, --5, --fast2, --fast-1, --fast=, --fast=0, --fast=x,
  and "=value" on any switch other than --fast/--threads
  (--best=3, --list=x, --rm=1, --quiet=2, --verbose=2, --keep=1, --force=1,
   --multiple=1, --compress=1, --stdout=1, --test=1, --content-size=0,
   --no-frame-crc=1, --favor-decSpeed=1, --sparse=on -> all "Incorrect parameters").
Long option names are case-sensitive (--Best, --KEEP, --Verbose all rejected).

## 6. Numeric parsing

### Compression level -N
-0 == -1 (level 1). Levels clamp silently at 12; no error, exit 0.
   med(200000B): -0/-1 -> 83479, -2 -> 50197, -3 -> 47122, -9 -> 29491,
   -10 -> 30344, -11 -> 26874, -12 -> 26211, -13/-14/-99/-100/-12345 -> 26211
Leading zeros fine: -0009 == -9. `-9-1` and `-f-` -> "Incorrect parameters" ('-' is
not a valid option char inside an aggregate).

### --fast / --fast=N
--fast (bare)  = acceleration 1 (cLevel -1). NOT the same bytes as -1
  (med: --fast -> 83481, -1 -> 83479).
--fast=0  -> "Incorrect parameters", exit 1.   --fast=  and --fast=x -> same error.
--fast=1x, --fast=1G -> ACCEPTED, trailing junk silently ignored (accel 1).
--fast=1K -> accel 1024 (K/M suffixes honoured).
Value is parsed as 32-bit with **silent wraparound**, then negated as a signed int:
  --fast=4294967295 -> behaves like level 1;  --fast=4294967294 -> level 2;
  --fast=42949672950 (mod 2^32 = 4294967286) -> level 10;
  --fast=4294967296 and --fast=18446744073709551616 (both == 0 mod 2^32)
      -> "Incorrect parameters", exit 1.
  No "overflow" diagnostic exists.

### -B (block size / block flags) — it is a mini sub-parser
`-B` alone: accepted, no-op, no message.
Digits: value must be 4..7 (predefined) or >= 32 (explicit bytes). 0..3 and 8..31 ->
  "Incorrect parameters", exit 1.
  -B4 -> b'using blocks of size 64 KB \\n'      -B5 -> 256 KB
  -B6 -> 1024 KB                               -B7 -> 4096 KB (default)
  -B32 -> b'using blocks of size 32 bytes \\n'  -B33 -> 33 bytes  -B64 -> 64 bytes
  -B65536 -> 64 KB    -B4194304 -> 4096 KB    -B4194305/-B100000000 -> 4096 KB (clamped)
  -B64K/-B64KB/-B64KiB -> 64 KB    -B1M -> 1024 KB    -B64MB -> 4096 KB (clamped)
  -B4294967296 -> "Incorrect parameters" (wraps to 0)
Letters: I = block independence (default), D = block dependency, X = block checksum.
  Any other letter is NOT an error: the -B loop ends and the remaining characters are
  re-parsed as ordinary short options in the same token. Hence:
    -Bd = -B -d   (switched to decompress; exit 44 on plain input)
    -Bb = -B -b   (benchmark mode!)     -Bi = -B -i
    -Bx, -BJ -> "Incorrect parameters" (x/J are not valid options)
  Order/mixing is free: -B4D, -BD4, -B65536D all give 64 KB + dependency; -B7X, -BXD ok.
  -B64G -> prints 'using blocks of size 64 bytes ' THEN "Incorrect parameters", exit 1.

### -T / --threads
-T with no digits, -T0 = auto. -T1 .. -T99999 all accepted, exit 0 (no clamp message).
-Tx / -T0x -> "Incorrect parameters" (trailing char parsed as an option).
-T1v -> accepted (v = verbose).
-T4294967296 -> accepted (wraps to 0 = auto).
--threads=N is STRICT and has its own messages:
  --threads=0/1/... ok.  --threads=  -> ok (0).  --threads=K -> ok (0).
  suffixes accepted: 1K 1KB 1KiB 1M 1MB 1MiB   (uppercase only)
  --threads=1k, =1kb, =1G, =1KX, =-1, =+1, =' 1' ->
     stderr b'error: only numeric values with optional suffixes K, KB, KiB, M, MB, MiB are allowed \\n', exit 1
  --threads (no '='), --threads2 ->
     stderr b'error: command cannot be separated from its argument by another command \\n', exit 1

### -i / -b / -e (benchmark)
Only **-b** activates benchmark mode; `-e` / `-i` alone do not.
-i (bare)=0, -i0, -i1, -i99, -i1K all accepted. -i1G -> "Incorrect parameters".
-b/-b0/-b9 ok; -b1 -e3 runs levels 1..3. Benchmark report goes to **stdout**, the
progress lines to stderr. Sample stdout row:
  b' /-in.txt            :        36 ->        22 (1.636), 201.1 MB/s ...'
`-e0` alone (no -b) is accepted and just compresses.

## 7. Aggregated short flags

Short options aggregate freely and numbers may be embedded anywhere:
  -9f, -f9, -kf, -zf, -dcfm, -cdf, -tv, -1v, -v1 all work.
Options with an attached value consume the digits that follow them, then parsing
continues with the next character of the same token (see -B/-T above).
-D takes the REST of the token if non-empty (`-Ddict.bin`, `-fD dict.bin`,
`-cD dict.bin`), otherwise the NEXT argv element unconditionally:
  `-D -c in.txt` -> dictionary name is "-c":
      stderr b'Compressed filename will be : in.txt.lz4 \\n-c: No such file or directory \\nError 27 : Dictionary error : could not open dictionary file \\n'
      exit 27
  `-D` as last argv element -> badusage, exit 1 (also `-c in.txt -D`).

## 8. Special argv tokens

"" (empty string) is a FILENAME (the empty name):
  `executable ""`   -> stderr b'Compressed filename will be : .lz4 \\n: No such file or directory \\n', exit 1
  `executable "" -c`-> stderr b': No such file or directory \\n', exit 1
"-"  = stdin (as input) / stdout (as output). `executable -` == no-args behaviour.
"stdin" = stdin, "stdout" = stdout, "null" = discard. Case-SENSITIVE:
  "NULL", "Stdout" are ordinary filenames (files were actually created).
"--" = end-of-options separator. Everything after it is a filename, INCLUDING "-"
  and a second "--":
  `executable --`              -> compress stdin->stdout, exit 0
  `executable -- -c in.txt`    -> stderr b'-c: No such file or directory \\n', exit 1
  `executable -c -- -`         -> stderr b'-: No such file or directory \\n', exit 1
  `executable -- --`           -> stderr b'Compressed filename will be : --.lz4 \\n--: No such file or directory \\n', exit 1
  `executable -c in.txt --`    -> works (the trailing -- is consumed, not a filename)
Options may appear AFTER filenames: `-1v in.txt out.lz4 -f` works.

## 9. Positional arguments

Slot 1 = input, slot 2 = output. With -c/--stdout the output slot is already taken,
so slot 2 becomes "extra".
Extra positional handling (message uses stderr):
  WITHOUT -f : b"Error : <name> won't be used ! Do you want multiple input files (-m) ? \\n"
               exit **1**, operation aborted, only the FIRST extra reported.
  WITH    -f : b"Warning : <name> won't be used ! Do you want multiple input files (-m) ? \\n"
               exit **0**, one line per extra, operation proceeds.
Examples:
  `-c in.txt out.bin`            -> Error, exit 1
  `-c -f in.txt out.bin`         -> Warning, exit 0 (frame on stdout)
  `in.txt out.bin extra1 extra2` -> Error on extra1, exit 1
  `-f p1 p2 p3`                  -> Warning p3, exit 0
  `-f p1 p2 p3 p4`               -> Warning p3, Warning p4, exit 0
With -m every positional is an input (no warnings). --list implies -m.

## 10. Automatic output filename

With exactly one filename and no output filename, the name is DERIVED even when
stdout is a redirected file (it does not default to stdout):
  `executable in.txt >out 2>err` -> creates in.txt.lz4, stderr starts with
     b'Compressed filename will be : in.txt.lz4 \\n'
Only when the input is stdin does output default to stdout.
Decompression with no '.lz4' suffix and no output name:
  `-d plain.dat` -> stderr b'Cannot determine an output filename \\n' + badusage, exit 1
  `-d plain.dat pout` -> proceeds (then b'Error 44 : Unrecognized header ...', exit 44)

## 11. Mode selection & precedence

Last mode-setting flag wins (-z compress, -d/-t decompress, --list list):
  `-d -z -c f.lz4` -> compresses (double-wrapped frame)
  `-z -d -c f.lz4` -> decompresses
  `-t --list f.lz4` -> lists ;  `--list -t f.lz4` -> decompresses **to stdout**
QUIRK: in multiple-input mode (-m, or -r, or implied by --list) `-t` writes the
decompressed data to **stdout** instead of discarding it:
  `-m -t c1.lz4` -> stdout = b'hello world hello world hello world\\n', exit 0, no file created.
`-c -t f.lz4` and `-t -c f.lz4` behave as plain test (stderr 'decoded 36 bytes').

## 12. argv[0]-driven default mode

Rule (verified): let base = basename(argv[0]). base "matches" token T iff
base starts with T and the next character is '\\0' or '.'  (case-SENSITIVE).
  T = "lz4cat" -> mode = decompress + write to stdout + pass-through of non-lz4
                  data + quiet (no stderr).
  T = "unlz4"  -> mode = decompress.
  anything else (lz4, lz4c, foo, LZ4, LZ4CAT, UNLZ4, mylz4cat, lz4catx, unlz4-)
                  -> mode = compress (auto: .lz4 input still decompresses).
Evidence (input plain.dat = 36B text, always `-c plain.dat`):
  lz4cat, /x/y/lz4cat, lz4cat.exe, lz4cat.EXE, lz4cat., lz4cat.foo, lz4cat.ex,
  lz4cat.exe.exe -> stdout = raw 36 bytes, exit 0
  unlz4, /a/b/unlz4, unlz4.exe, unlz4.EXE, unlz4.zzz -> exit 44,
     b'Error 44 : Unrecognized header : file cannot be decoded \\n'
  lz4, lz4.exe, lz4c, foo, LZ4, LZ4CAT, LZ4CAT.EXE, UNLZ4, Lz4Cat, mylz4cat,
     xunlz4, lz4catx, unlz4-, lz4cat-, 'lz4cat ', ' lz4cat', '', -lz4cat
     -> stdout = 41-byte lz4 frame, exit 0
lz4cat's pass-through is reproducible with plain lz4 via `-dcf`:
  `-dc plain.dat`  -> exit 44 'Error 44 : Unrecognized header ...'
  `-dcf plain.dat` -> exit 0, raw bytes copied to stdout, stderr empty

## 13. Verbosity

Effective level = 2 + (#-v/#--verbose) - (#-q/#--quiet); -h/-H/-V ignore it.
level 2 (default, single file): 'Compressed filename will be : X \\n',
  progress '\\rRead : 0 MiB   ==> 113.89%   \\r' + 79 spaces + '\\r' then
  b'Compressed 36 bytes into 41 bytes ==> 113.89%\\n'
level 3 (-v): adds banner b'*** lz4 v1.10.0 64-bit multithread, by Yann Collet ***\\n',
  b'Using 55 threads for compression \\n', and b'Done in 0.00 s ==> 0.22 MiB/s  (cpu load : 100%)\\n'
level 4 (-vv): banner + b'_POSIX_C_SOURCE defined: 200809L\\n_POSIX_VERSION defined: 200809L\\n' ...
level 1 (-q): only warnings/errors, e.g. b'nosuchfile.txt: No such file or directory \\n'
level 0 (-qq/-qqq): completely silent, exit codes unchanged.
-m suppresses the per-file level-2 chatter entirely (success => empty stderr).

## 14. Overwrite prompt (byte-exact)

Single-file mode, level >= 2, output exists, no -f:
  stderr: b'ow.txt.lz4 already exists; do you want to overwrite (y/N) ?     not overwritten  \\n'
  (i.e. prompt "...(y/N) ? " then, after reading EOF/'n', "    not overwritten  \\n")
  exit 1.  Answering 'y' on stdin -> exit 0 and file overwritten. 'n' -> exit 1.
Level <= 1 (e.g. -q, or -m at default level): no prompt, just
  b'ow.txt.lz4 already exists; not overwritten  \\n', exit 1 (per file).
